record.paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
record.original_question: Given an asymptotically flat Einstein initial data set (M,g,K) and a future trapped surface Sigma, must there exist an apparent horizon inside Sigma, meaning a closed spacelike 2-surface with one future null mean curvature equal to zero?

evidence.quote: show there is an apparent horizon inside

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g,K)$ be an asymptotically flat initial data set for the Einstein equations, where $M$ is a smooth $3$-manifold, $g$ is a complete Riemannian metric on $M$, and $K$ is a symmetric $(0,2)$-tensor on $M$ playing the role of the second fundamental form. For a closed orientable two-sided surface $\Sigma\subset M$ with outward unit normal $
u$, induced mean curvature $H_\Sigma$ (with respect to $
u$) and $\mathrm{tr}_\Sigma K := \mathrm{tr}_g K - K(
u,
u)$, define the future outgoing null expansion $	heta^+ := H_\Sigma + \mathrm{tr}_\Sigma K$ and the future ingoing null expansion $	heta^- := -H_\Sigma + \mathrm{tr}_\Sigma K$. The surface $\Sigma$ is called future trapped if $	heta^+<0$ and $	heta^-<0$ everywhere on $\Sigma$, and is called a (future) marginally outer trapped surface (apparent horizon) if $	heta^+\equiv 0$.

Suppose $\Sigma\subset M$ is a closed future trapped surface in such an asymptotically flat initial data set $(M,g,K)$. Must there exist a closed embedded marginally outer trapped surface $\Sigma'\subset M$ contained in the compact region bounded by $\Sigma$ and the asymptotic end (i.e., "inside" $\Sigma$)?
artifact.category_tag: Marginally outer trapped surfaces in general relativity
artifact.status_search_result: The existence of a marginally outer trapped surface (apparent horizon) inside any future trapped surface in an asymptotically flat initial data set was established by Andersson–Metzger in dimension 3, and extended to dimensions up to 7 by Eichmair using the Plateau-problem/Jang-equation approach. These results provide the MOTS Existence Theorem, confirming the existence of an outermost MOTS bounding the trapped region.

status_evidence.title: The Area of Horizons and the Trapped Region
status_evidence.snippet: Andersson and Metzger establish existence of an outermost MOTS in 3-dimensional initial data sets containing a trapped surface.
status_evidence.claim: Existence of an apparent horizon inside any trapped region was proved by Andersson–Metzger.

status_evidence.title: The Plateau problem for marginally outer trapped surfaces
status_evidence.snippet: Eichmair extends MOTS existence using Plateau-problem methods to dimensions 3 ≤ n ≤ 7.
status_evidence.claim: The MOTS existence theorem holds in dimensions up to 7 (Eichmair).

status_evidence.title: The trapped region (Andersson)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey establishing the existence of outermost MOTS bounding the trapped region in asymptotically flat data containing a trapped surface.
status_evidence.claim: Apparent horizons exist inside any trapped surface in asymptotically flat data.
